passages.context: The general chapter note and the notes on 15:1-11, 15:3-7, and 15:9-11 were inspected for the bounded identification of received tradition. The notes distinguish Paul's recalled common tradition from his own formulation and identify the language of 15:3-7 as drawn from older credal formulas centered on Jesus' death, burial, resurrection, appearances, and fulfillment of scripture; 15:9-11 is treated as Paul's parenthetical self-defense concerning grace, qualification, and labor.

passages.context: The complete introduction was inspected for bounded historical orientation. It distinguishes the Gospel's anonymity and ancient manuscript heading from its traditional attribution to John Mark and Papias's Petrine connection; it reports the traditional placement shortly before AD 70 at Rome while noting a modern proposal of an unknown Hellenistic Jewish Christian, possibly in Syria, shortly after 70. It also situates Mark 7:24-37 within the Gospel's rare movements into Gentile territory.
